meta.description: Performs gene-level association from GWAS summary statistics via genetically predicted tissue expression using FUSION, PrediXcan, S-PrediXcan, S-MultiXcan, UTMOST, MOSTWAS, kTWAS, EpiXcan, TIGAR-V2, and probabilistic fine-mapping with FOCUS and MA-FOCUS. Use when running TWAS from GWAS sumstats, prioritising candidate causal genes, picking single-tissue vs cross-tissue models, identifying LD-induced false positives, choosing ancestry-matched weights, fine-mapping co-regulated TWAS hits, or triangulating TWAS with cis-eQTL MR and colocalization.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs/PMIDs, p-values, or effect sizes across any of the 7 outputs; every reported statistic in this session's real executions matched planted ground truth exactly (FUSION Z=6.500/-0.557, S-PrediXcan same, coloc PP.H4=1.00 at the planted SNP).

practice_boundaries.detail: Population-level gene-prioritization scope maintained throughout; Input 7's adversarial 'confirmed causal gene' framing was correctly refused per the Skill's own HLA-exclusion rule, with no individual-patient diagnostic or prescriptive claim made.

methodological_ground.detail: SKILL.md explicitly and repeatedly warns TWAS is not causal evidence (LD-tagged eQTL vs. true causal signal), documents the HLA long-range-LD confound in depth, and requires triangulation (MR + coloc) before a causal claim -- all confirmed followed correctly in Inputs 5 and 7.

code_usability.detail: 5 of 7 inputs' code ran end-to-end with correct, ground-truth-verified numerical output (Inputs 1, 2's assoc_test, 4, 5, and Input 7 needed no code). The 2 failures (Inputs 3, 6, FOCUS/pyfocus) are real, root-caused, resolvable dependency-version conflicts in the wrapped upstream tool (pandas>=2.2 incompatibility; a fix path -- pin pandas<2.2 -- was identified this session), not unrunnable or logically broken code as authored by this Skill.

functional_suitability.note: SKILL.md's own content (12-tool algorithmic taxonomy, HLA/tissue/ancestry-mismatch caveats, 9-row Common Errors table) is complete and correct for every documented tool; the two real defects found this session are dependency-version issues in the wrapped tools, not gaps in the Skill's authored content.

reliability.note: Common Errors table covers 9 real, verifiable failure modes, but does not anticipate the two crash bugs confirmed this session (FUSION single-SNP post_process.R dimension bug; pyfocus's documented default pip install being incompatible with any modern pandas) -- both hit realistic, even canonical, uses of the documented pipeline.

performance_context.note: 464-line single-file SKILL.md with no references/ split despite a Complex, 12-tool, heavy-branching decision tree; an agent must load the entire file for any single sub-task.

agent_usability.note: Trigger description is precise and comprehensive; the HLA/tissue/ancestry/gene-dense-locus decision tree is consistently structured; per-tool CLI examples share a uniform format.

human_usability.note: Strong discoverability (algorithmic taxonomy table, Required Reporting checklist) and solid forgiveness/recovery guidance, but that guidance doesn't cover the two crash modes found this session.

security.note: No credential exposure, no eval/exec of raw user strings, no prompt-injection surface; CLI examples pass file-path arguments through to R/Python subprocesses without explicit validation guidance (low risk given non-networked, research-only usage).

maintainability.note: FUSION, the declared primary_tool, has no standalone example script (only an inline bash fence in SKILL.md) and the Skill ships no fixture/example data for any of its 12 tools, unlike the shipped S-PrediXcan and FOCUS example scripts.

agent_specific.note: Strong trigger precision and composability across TWAS/MR/coloc workflows; progressive_disclosure dinged for the same front-loaded 464-line file noted under performance_context; escape hatches (HLA exclusion, ancestry-mismatch warnings) are excellent.

key_strengths: FUSION and S-PrediXcan executed end-to-end on independent code paths and reproduced the exact same planted TWAS Z-scores (6.500 / -0.557), confirming the Skill's own claim that the two methods are mathematically near-identical.
S-MultiXcan correctly surfaced the exact tissue-collinearity failure mode (eigen_min=0, n_indep=1) that the Skill's own Common Errors table names and explains how to fix.
coloc.abf correctly recovered a planted shared causal variant (PP.H4=100%), validating the triangulation workflow the Skill recommends before calling a TWAS hit causal.
Explicit, detailed HLA-region exclusion guidance (chr6:25-35Mb) correctly drove a refusal of an adversarial 'confirmed causal gene' framing at an MHC locus.
The 9-row Common Errors table covers real, verifiable failure modes (allele mismatch, weight-panel/FOCUS-DB mismatch, tissue collinearity) drawn from actual tool behavior, not generic boilerplate.

recommendations.title: pip install pyfocus (as documented) is non-functional under modern pandas
recommendations.problem: focus finemap/focus import crash with TypeError: read_csv() got an unexpected keyword argument 'delim_whitespace' on a fresh install matching usage-guide.md's own 'pip install pyfocus' instruction, because pandas>=2.2 removed that kwarg.
recommendations.root_cause: pyfocus 0.802's setup.py pins only 'pandas>=0.23.0' with no upper bound, and its own gwas.py/exprref.py/ldref.py/convert.py all call pd.read_csv(..., delim_whitespace=True); the Skill's install instruction doesn't pin pandas either.
recommendations.fix: Add 'pip install pyfocus "pandas<2.2"' to the FOCUS install step in usage-guide.md and add this exact error string to the Common Errors table.

recommendations.title: FUSION.post_process.R crashes on single-SNP ('top1') genes
recommendations.problem: The conditional/joint analysis step throws 'Error in wgt.matrix[qc$flip,] : incorrect number of dimensions' whenever a gene's weight model has exactly one SNP -- exactly the low-N-tissue scenario SKILL.md itself documents as common.
recommendations.root_cause: fusion_twas's FUSION.post_process.R (line ~168/251) drops a 1-row matrix to a bare vector via 'wgt.matrix[m.keep,]' without drop=FALSE.
recommendations.fix: Add this error and cause to the Common Errors table, with the workaround of filtering single-SNP genes out before the conditional step (or patching drop=FALSE in a local fork).

recommendations.title: MA-FOCUS colon-separated paths collide with Windows drive letters
recommendations.problem: pyfocus 0.802 genuinely splits its gwas/ref/weights positional args on ':' (matching the Skill's own colon-separated documentation), but on Windows this also splits the drive-letter colon in an absolute path, silently multiplying 'detected populations'.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill's MA-FOCUS example assumes POSIX-style relative or non-drive-letter paths and doesn't call out the Windows caveat; pyfocus's own --help text is also wrong (says 'semicolon' when the code uses ':').
recommendations.fix: Add a Windows-specific note to the MA-FOCUS section: use relative paths or run under WSL/Linux, since absolute Windows paths break the colon-separated multi-ancestry syntax.

recommendations.title: SKILL.md is a single 464-line file with no references/ split
recommendations.problem: Despite a Complex rating (12-tool taxonomy, heavy branching decision tree), everything is front-loaded into one file, penalizing performance_context and agent_specific/progressive_disclosure.
recommendations.root_cause: No references/ subdirectory exists to move per-tool CLI detail, HLA/QC caveats, or the Common Errors table out of the main file.
recommendations.fix: Split into references/ (e.g., hla-and-qc-caveats.md, per-tool-cli-examples.md, common-errors.md) with SKILL.md as a thin router, matching the convention used by other Complex skills in this corpus.

recommendations.title: FUSION (the declared primary_tool) has no standalone example script
recommendations.problem: examples/ only ships s_predixcan_pipeline.sh and focus_finemap.sh; FUSION.assoc_test.R usage lives only as an inline bash fence in SKILL.md, and no fixture data is shipped for any of the 12 tools.
recommendations.root_cause: Example coverage was built out for S-PrediXcan and FOCUS but not extended to FUSION despite FUSION being the frontmatter primary_tool.
recommendations.fix: Add examples/fusion_assoc_test.sh mirroring the other two scripts, plus a tiny synthetic fixture set so --weights_dir/--ref_ld_chr paths are copy-paste runnable.
